unit: a named relative that residue reads point at, at E < 1e-05
not_a_risk_assessment: this is a triage order for a person's attention, built from four measured quantities. It is not a probability of harm, not a clinical finding, and not a statement that anything here infects anyone. Nothing in it scores novelty: an index can say whether something is already known and cannot say whether it is new

formula_terms.weight: log1p(residue reads) over log1p(the largest subject in this run); an ordering within the run, never an abundance claim
formula_terms.distance: 1 - identity ramped from 40% to 100%. 40% is where this repo's own BLAST ground truth puts the chance band for a short query, so below it an identity is not a distance
formula_terms.host_term: the matched record's group weight, damped towards unknown by a confidence that falls with distance and with short alignments. Distance raises interest and lowers host confidence at once, and this is where that tension is paid for rather than hidden
formula_terms.only_in_residue: 0.6 if the already-identified pile points at the same subject, because then it is something we have, seen again

bacteriophage.label: bacteriophage
bacteriophage.reading: infects bacteria. The expected background of a wastewater RNA virome and the dominant signal in this library.

plant.label: plant
plant.reading: infects plants. Abundant in sewage from diet and runoff.

fungal_or_protist.label: fungal or protist
fungal_or_protist.reading: infects fungi, amoebae or other protists.

invertebrate.label: invertebrate
invertebrate.reading: infects insects or other invertebrates. Worth noting because arbovirus relatives sit here and because an insect virus in sewage is ordinary.

vertebrate_non_human.label: non-human vertebrate
vertebrate_non_human.reading: infects vertebrates other than humans. Livestock and wildlife viruses, which is where most spillover ancestry sits.

human_associated.label: human-associated
human_associated.reading: a family that includes viruses infecting humans. The group a person should look at first, and the one where the damping below matters most.

unknown_host.label: host not placed
unknown_host.reading: the table could not place this record's name. Weighted in the middle on purpose: an unplaceable name is not evidence of safety, and weighting it at zero would hide exactly the rows this project exists to find.

host_table.coverage_note: an unplaced name is grouped unknown_host and weighted in the middle, never at zero

kind_summary.unit: residue MATES with a significant named relative, at E < 1e-05

putative_phage.label: putative phage
putative_phage.reading: the matched record is a virus and its own name says phage

virus_no_phage_signal.label: virus, nothing says phage
virus_no_phage_signal.reading: the matched record is a virus from the viral index, and nothing in its name marks it as a phage. An absence of evidence, not a finding that it is not one

putative_bacterial.label: putative bacterial or archaeal
putative_bacterial.reading: the matched record is a protein of a named prokaryote, not of a virus. A prophage protein would look exactly like this

cellular_kind_not_placed.label: something living, kind not placed
cellular_kind_not_placed.reading: the record is a cellular protein and the table could not place its domain from the organism name

putative_eukaryotic.label: putative eukaryotic
putative_eukaryotic.reading: the matched record is a protein of a named plant, fungus, animal or protist. In a wastewater metatranscriptome this is diet, plant matter and the organisms living in the works, not a finding

known_pile_control.reading: the same count on reads the cascade already identified. It is the scale the residue's figure is read against: these are reads with a known relative by construction, and even they do not all have a significant one at this threshold

kind_summary.caveat: phage against bacterial is the hardest of the three and the page says so. Prophages sit inside bacterial genomes, so a protein can honestly be both, and at the identities in this residue - a few dozen amino acids at around half identity - neither the record nor the alignment settles it. These buckets describe the RECORD that was matched. They are not a call on the read.

denominator_note: residue mates searched by the per-read report (reads.jsonl), not the residual pairs of the cascade block: the numerator counts mates in that same sample

scope.scope: the per-read report's block sample of the residue

interval_note: shares of the residue carry a Wilson interval widened by 1.09x, the measured design effect of reading a contiguous block of the FASTQ (results/block_position_bias/)
blind_to: anything below about 1 read pair in a million, which is most of what a surveillance tool would want to catch early
anything whose nearest relative is further than roughly 10-20% divergence, because then there is no named relative to rank at all
any subject the keyword table could not place, which is counted above and ranked as unknown rather than as safe

host_confidence_summary.best_fields_are_independent: best_identity_percent and best_aligned_aa (= longest_alignment_aa) are maxima over the rows taken separately and are usually different subjects. Do not print them as one match. The identity's own alignment length is closest_row_aligned_aa.
host_confidence_summary.reading: how much of the matched record's host group transfers to the reads. Built from identity and aligned length. If the maximum is low, no relative in this residue is close enough for its host to mean anything, and the host colours on this page are labels on the database rather than claims about the sample
